Operator: Good day, and welcome to the TeleMedia Corp Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during this time, you will need to press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, please press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to TeleMedia Corp's Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Marcus Hale, Chief Financial Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report our results for Q2. We achieved robust revenue growth and margin expansion, which reflects our strong execution in a dynamic market. We are particularly excited about the initial performance of our NovaStream fiber broadband service and its rapid customer uptake across key regions. Our investments in network densification and spectrum optimization are also paying off, driving increased customer satisfaction and loyalty. Furthermore, we have focused on operational efficiencies and cost discipline, which has allowed us to maintain profitability amid competitive pressures. Finally, our strategic focus remains on accelerating fiber deployments and converging telecom with media services to capture long-term share in broadband and streaming.

Marcus Hale: Thank you, Elena. Turning to the financials, our revenue for the quarter was $28.4 billion, representing a 7% increase year-over-year. Our adjusted EBITDA was $7.1 billion, with a margin of 25%. We continue to manage our expenses effectively and are on track to meet our financial targets for the year. Our capital expenditures were $3.3 billion, primarily driven by investments in our fiber-to-the-home network expansion and 5G enhancements.

Let me provide more detail on some of our key operational pillars starting with our fiber buildout program, which is central to our long-term growth strategy in telecom and media. Our FTTH network delivers multi-gigabit symmetric speeds, supporting not only top-tier broadband but also high-end video streaming, cloud gaming, and 5G fixed-wireless backhaul. We're deploying XGS-PON technology throughout our markets, with early 10G PON rollouts in priority areas to prepare for bandwidth-heavy uses like 8K video and AI content processing.

On the numbers, we passed 1.8 million additional homes this quarter, lifting total homes passed to 12.5 million—a 28% jump year-over-year and 15% sequentially from Q1. This exceeds our annual target of 6.5 to 7 million new homes passed. For subscribers, we gained 650,000 fiber broadband customers, pushing the total to 4.2 million, up 32% from last year. That's a 33.6% penetration on homes passed, improving 250 basis points from the prior quarter and continuing our streak of 10 quarters of rising take rates.

Momentum is strong, with Q2's average monthly take rate at 4.2%, boosted by direct sales efforts, online campaigns, and win-back promotions against rivals like Comcast Xfinity and Charter Spectrum. Fiber ARPU reached $112, up 7% year-over-year, thanks to packaging 2 Gbps symmetric plans with our NovaStream media platform, now featuring ad-supported options from Paramount+ and Peacock. Monthly churn held at a leading 0.8%, far below the cable peer average of 1.4%, aided by AI-powered network operations and business support systems.

Construction advanced with 22,000 route miles of fiber laid, 85% aerial and the rest underground or micro-trenched, keeping CapEx around $850 per passing—a 12% efficiency gain year-over-year. This comes from pole-sharing deals with utilities such as Duke Energy and Entergy, cutting make-ready expenses by 20%. We brought online 1,200 new optical line terminals handling GPON and XGS-PON at ratios up to 1:64 for future scalability. Permitting times have improved to under 45 days on average, following proactive work with local governments tied to BEAD mapping.

Expansion focused on three regions to meet RDOF and CAF II obligations. In the Southeast Sunbelt, 45% of builds, we passed 850,000 homes in Florida, Georgia, and the Carolinas, including Atlanta and Orlando MSAs. We're surpassing AT&T Fiber in rural outskirts with 40% take rates in established areas, highlighted by a $150 million REIT joint venture for 500,000 MDUs by year-end. The Midwest rural markets took 30% of effort, adding 450,000 homes in Ohio, Indiana, and Michigan using $220 million RDOF funding. Take rates there reached 38%, displacing DSL and T-Mobile Home Internet, with Nokia Wi-Fi 7 customer premises equipment lifting NPS to 92%. Northeast and Texas claimed 25%, passing 500,000 homes in Dallas-Fort Worth and Philadelphia, undercutting Verizon Fios at $79.99 for 1 Gig symmetric—20% cheaper. DFW 10G PON tests show 50% upgrades to 2 Gig within 90 days.

This is reshaping our media business, with fiber enabling low-latency NovaStream SVOD at 1.8 million subs—43% of fiber broadband users—for a 25% ARPU boost via 4K/8K bundles. We're gearing up for IPTV growth through Disney ESPN+ partnerships on our PON setup. Starlink poses little threat in our areas; their 100-200 Mbps model can't compete with our 2-10 Gbps scale, backed by $5 billion liquidity for more builds.

For Q3, expect 1.9 to 2.1 million homes passed and 700,000 net adds, with full-year CapEx at $3.2 to 3.4 billion, 72% fiber. Take rates aim for 35% by Q4, driving fiber revenue to $5.1 billion annually—45% of broadband and adding 300 basis points to EBITDA margins. We're set for 20 million homes passed by 2026, generating $2 billion in free cash flow.

Next, on balance sheet strength, particularly debt levels and leverage. At quarter-end June 30, gross debt was $52.4 billion: $28.2 billion senior unsecured notes, $15.1 billion term loans, $9.1 billion secured against towers and international fiber. Netting $4.7 billion cash and equivalents—lifted by 5G ramp and streaming synergies—net debt is $47.7 billion.

TTM adjusted EBITDA hit $15.2 billion, up 8% year-over-year from U.S. wireless postpaid ARPU at $58.50, 450,000 European broadband adds via Virgin Media O2, and 12% media ad growth on Peacock programmatic. This yields a 3.1x net debt-to-EBITDA ratio, down from 3.5x year-end 2023 and 4.2x post-C-band auctions.

Year-to-date debt paydown totaled $3.8 billion, including full €1.5 billion Eurobond repayment at 2.75%, swapped for 4.25% dollar notes. Weighted average debt cost is 4.1%, 72% fixed, 5.8-year maturity—shielding us versus peers' floating exposure amid Fed hikes.

U.S. ops (55% EBITDA) at under 2.8x leverage, via FiOS at 65% Northeast coverage and 85% 5G Ultra Wideband. Europe at 3.6x from €4 billion UK/Germany FTTH, but churn at 0.9% and 15% broadband growth speed payback. Latin America Claro JV at 3.4x, improving on Brazil ARPU +11%. Asia-Pacific at 2.4x from tower deals like Crown Castle.

We're balancing deleveraging with $18 billion 2024 CapEx—65% for 5G SA, Open RAN with Nokia/Ericsson cutting opex 20%, edge for media. $1.2 billion from asset sales like Spanish cable, plus Warner Bros. Discovery licensing, no strain. Interest coverage 5.2x, above 4.0x covenants. Expect 2.9x by year-end, targeting 2.5-3.0x like Verizon, for M&A in media-telecom like Liberty Global deals.

Now, shifting to net subscriber additions by segment—residential and business—which highlight our market share gains against streamers like Netflix, FWA from T-Mobile/Verizon, and Starlink.

In residential, we posted net adds of 285,000 this quarter, on pace for full-year mirroring last year's 1.35 million surge—18% above 2022's 1.14 million. Strongest since mid-2021, from fiber expansions, bundles, retention.

Broadband led with FTTH to 28 million homes passed, 42% penetration up from 38%. Northeast/Mid-Atlantic GigaFiber added 120,000, via $20/month gigabit discounts, gaining 2.5 points vs. Spectrum in Philly/Boston.

Mobile postpaid residential adds 95,000 via Total Connect bundle—5G unlimited + NovaStream+ live/on-demand/FAST. Bundled ARPU $142, +4%, churn 0.75% via AI personalization cutting disconnects 22%.

West Coast +45% YoY, FWA aiding suburbs; rural South +12% countered Starlink with mmWave hybrid 25,000 adds. Sequential +12% from Q1 on holiday bundles, Roku/Fire TV integrations.

Business netted 52,000 adds quarterly, full-year track to 215,000—27% above 2022's 169,000. Now 14% revenue, 52% EBITDA margins from enterprise/SMB.

18 enterprise deals $450 million recurring, private 5G for Hollywood/NYC studios—Disney 4K encoding 8,000 seats. SD-WAN +35% vs. AT&T MPLS.

SMB +42% to 32,000, Business Essential UCaaS/cyber/IoT, $1,800/month avg +15%, retail/media signage.

Midwest +30% logistics 5G, Southeast +22% office returns. Churn 1.1%, 98% three-year renewals. 5G slicing AR/VR media 5,000 adds. Business ARPU $1,250/month +7%, slicing/security.

Total 337,000 quarterly, 1.565 million yearly pace—20% YoY, base to 68.2 million. Converged strategy: $12 billion CapEx 85% fiber/5G, Warner FAST, 2.4 GHz FWA for unconnected homes. Offset 3% linear TV drop with 25% streaming growth.

Q1 2025 guide 250-300k residential, 45-55k business, stable economy no auctions.

Finally, free cash flow: $2.4 billion in Q2, full-year pace to $8.7 billion—18% above 2022's $7.4 billion, beating $8.0 billion guide. Up 12% from prior Q2 $2.1 billion.

FCF = adjusted OCF minus CapEx. OCF $6.0 billion quarterly pace to $24.1 billion yearly +14%, EBITDA $8.1 billion quarterly to $32.5 billion +16% on wireless $11.3 billion quarterly +9%, ARPU $52.30 +4% 5G plans; broadband $3.2 billion +22% FTTH 55% coverage, FWA 300k adds quarterly.

CapEx $3.85 billion quarterly to $15.4 billion or 17.5% revenue, down from 19.8%, 5G SA maturity. Network $2.3 billion quarterly 60%, Open RAN Nokia/Rakuten -15% costs. Media $450 million edge for NexStream+ <10ms sports vs. Netflix/Prime.

North America $1.8 billion quarterly 82%, C-band 70% util, Dish synergies. EMEA $300 million +25% 4G/5G UK/Germany tower American Tower. APAC $100 million 5G mmWave Japan/Indonesia FX hit.

Utilization: $8.7 billion yearly—37% or $3.2 billion debt reduction to 2.1x from 2.6x, $1.5 billion high-coupon refi <4%. 32% or $2.8 billion returns: dividend +8% $0.65/share 4.2% yield, 45 million shares $1.7 billion $38 avg. 23% or $2.0 billion growth: $800 million spectrum, $500 million StreamForge $4.2 billion SVOD bolt-on vs. Peacock. 8% or $700 million cash to $5.2 billion M&A like Vodafone-Three.

FY2024 guide $9.5-10.0 billion FCF +9-15%, CapEx 16-17% revenues, AI slicing enterprise, GenAI media. Vs. Starlink rural, Charter mobile.

This positions TeleMedia as a cash engine post-5G build.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the fiber buildout momentum and how take rates are trending versus competitors?

Elena Vasquez: Certainly, Emily. As Marcus detailed, our 33.6% penetration and 4.2% monthly take rates are accelerating, outpacing AT&T and cable in key markets like Southeast and Midwest. Bundles with NovaStream are key, and Q3 guidance reflects continued strength.

Marcus Hale: To add, our $850 per passing efficiency and regional wins—like 40% in Sunbelt mature areas and 38% Midwest rural—give us edge over Fios and Spectrum pricing.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Patel with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Patel: Hi, thanks for taking my question. Could you elaborate on your plans for free cash flow utilization amid high CapEx?

Marcus Hale: Yes, David. We're sticking to Grow, Optimize, Return: debt deleveraging to 2.9x year-end, dividends/buybacks yielding EPS lift, growth like spectrum and StreamForge, with cash buffer for M&A. FY24 guide $9.5-10 billion supports all, prioritizing shareholder returns post-fiber ramp.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Elena, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Elena Vasquez: Thank you. In closing, I am proud of our team's performance this quarter. We are well-positioned to continue delivering value to our customers and shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
